author: Mark Atwood
text: FRAMING CORRECTION 2026-05-12 (Mark, interactive after pointing out wrong-frame reasoning). Un-deferring this epic. The earlier 7-day defer was wrong-framed: the recorded trigger condition was 'concrete external consumer asks for an interop format,' which imports post-launch YAGNI logic into a prelaunch decision. Per the new AGENTS.md 'Project phase and decision framing' section: this workspace is prelaunch, designing for the eventual complete shape, and 'no concrete consumer is asking' is the default condition for this phase -- not a signal about whether the feature belongs. The substantive question is: what does the policy-data-storage architecture look like when complete? Two candidate completed shapes: (A) Rust-only -- workspace ships Rust validators + Rust constants for policy data; consumers who want a wire format roll their own adapter. Architecturally complete because policy IS code in this design; (B) Workspace prescribes a canonical wire format (one of OSCAL / SARIF / JSON Schema'd workspace shape / TOML-RON / etc.) -- workspace ships emit/parse for that format; policy data is interchange artifact independent of any specific consumer's runtime. Architecturally complete because policy is data with a defined schema. The earlier description's 'Prerequisites for making the call' section (concrete consumer use cases gathered, vendoring pressure assessed, cross-ecosystem compliance claims decided) is itself wrong-frame and should be ignored -- those gates are post-launch concerns. The real decision needs to be made on architectural-completeness grounds. Will surface to Mark for a substantive re-decision.
